newsitem.title: EGYPT: Turkey says defence ties with Israel not alliance.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says defence ties with Israel not alliance.

text.p: Turkey's defence minister said in remarks published on Thursday that his country's military ties with Israel were not directed against a third state, but tied them indirectly to Syrian support of Kurdish rebels.
Turhan Tayan also told the Egyptian government daily al-Ahram there was no "military alliance" between his country and Israel but only "training and cooperation agreements".
NATO member Turkey has signed two military accords with Israel allowing Israeli military jets to use Turkish airspace for training flights and to upgrade its own ageing F-4 fighters in Israel.
The two countries have also agreed to hold joint naval exercises. Such cooperation has angered and alarmed neighbouring Arab states.
"Arab states, which are concerned about our relations with Israel, should be concerned about terrorism," Tayan said.
"Neighbouring states... support terrorism that is directed against our country...Turkey does not care about those neighbours," he added.
When pressed to name these countries, Tayan said: "Syria. Yes, it is Syria... I am talking about facts. The terrorist leader (Abdullah Ocalan) is living in Syria."
More than 24,000 people have died since 1984 in fighting between the Turkish army and Ogalan's PKK, which wants to set up Kurdish self-rule in southeast Turkey.

Turkey said on Thursday it had withdrawn most of its 10,000 troops, whom it sent into northern Iraq, after a six-week campaign against the PKK rebels that angered the Arab world. The rebels use bases in the mountains there to strike into Turkey.
Tayan told the newspaper that his country wanted to cooperate with Israel because of the Jewish state's technological advances.

"If Israel's capabilities were owned by Iraq, we would have signed military cooperation agreements with Iraq. If Egypt had produced military aircraft, we would have purchased them from Egypt," Tayan said.

In the latest sign of Ankara's growing military ties with the Jewish state, security sources said five Turkish navy vessels docked in an Israeli port last week. They said the flotilla included a submarine, three small warships and a supply vessel.
Israel and Turkey have yet to set a date for their joint naval exercises. Media reports said the United States had agreed to join the manoeuvres in the eastern Mediterranean some time in the summer.
But Tayan denied the U.S. participation, saying, "There are no contacts between Turkey and America on this topic".
